subject: Acme Health SSQ: KMS custody, subprocessor role mapping, and dataflow illustration
messages:
From: Jill Ramos <jill.ramos@acmehealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Health DPO <dpo@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SSQ follow-up: KMS custody and subprocessor roles

Sean —

Thanks for the demo last week. Our info-sec team had a few follow-ups on the security questionnaire that were flagged as "requires evidence": specifically items 12, 14, and 19 (KMS key custody model, list of subprocessors with role mapping, and an updated dataflow diagram showing cross-border hops). Can you confirm what we can provide as evidence? A few specific asks: 

- A mapping that ties each subprocessor to the data handling role (ingest, inference, telemetry, backups).
- Whether any backups are stored in a different region and if so which subprocessors have access.
- Clarify the KMS model: are customer keys supported and do you offer escrow or split custody for enterprise customers?

We need these artifacts for our DPA review cycle (timeline: target sign by 6/18). Appreciate a pointer to any existing artifacts to avoid rework.

Regards,
Jill Ramos
Head of Security Programs
Acme Health

From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Jill Ramos <jill.ramos@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Jun 2025 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SSQ follow-up: KMS custody and subprocessor roles

Jill —

Thanks for the clear list. We can provide an annotated dataflow diagram, a subprocessor role matrix, and a KMS custody note. High-level answers now: 

- Subprocessor mapping: we classify subprocessors by function (ingest, model hosting/inference, telemetry/monitoring, backups/archival). I will attach a CSV mapping that ties vendor -> role -> access scope.
- Backups: backups for hosted customers are kept in the same cloud region by default; for cross-region replication we require explicit configuration and disclosure. We will call out any subprocessors that have replication access in the matrix.
- KMS: Redwood supports both platform-managed keys and customer-managed keys (CMKs) via standard KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS). For enterprise customers we offer an escrow/split custody option using an HSM third party — this is typically documented in a separate attestation; we can prepare wording and an example key custody diagram.

I'll loop Marcus for the dataflow artifact and Monica to sign off on the subprocessor CSV. Expect initial artifacts by EOD tomorrow (6/5).

Sean Gallagher
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Jun 2025 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: FW: SSQ follow-up: KMS custody and subprocessor roles

Team —

Attaching the first-pass artifacts for Acme: redwood_dataflow_v2.pdf (annotated dataflow showing tenant isolation, KV cache boundaries, and network egress), and kms_key_map.csv (exported mapping: key type, customer-managed? yes/no, KMS provider, which subprocessors have decryption access for operational use). I've also included a draft DPA redline with a proposed clause for escrow/split custody (dpa_redline_20250605.pdf).

Notes: 
- The dataflow highlights two places where telemetry (metrics/logs) are scrubbed to remove PII prior to reaching the monitoring pipeline. For customers needing more aggressive minimization we can suggest an in-path redaction proxy or dedicated telemetry subprocessor scoping.
- The kms_key_map explicitly marks backup decryption access as restricted to our archival subprocessor (ColdStore Inc.) which is US-only by default. Cross-region replication (EU) would add an EU archival subprocessor; we note that in the CSV.

Monica / Lauren: please review the matrix and the wording on the escrow paragraph (page 3 of the DPA redline). I flagged two TODOs in the PDF where legal input is required.

- Marcus
Principal Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Acme Health DPO <dpo@acmehealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Jill Ramos <jill.ramos@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Tom Hwang <tom.h@consultingco.io>
Date: Thu, 5 Jun 2025 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SSQ follow-up: KMS custody and subprocessor roles

Sean / Team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround, Marcus. A few clarifying questions from our side after reviewing the artifacts: 

1) The kms_key_map marks "operational decryption" for model hosting subprocessors. Can you confirm the circumstances where model hosting needs plaintext-derived keys versus encrypted-only flows (we're particularly concerned about inference requests that might require access to decrypted tokens or embeddings)?

2) The dataflow shows a monitoring tap that receives aggregated metrics. Does any PII ever transit that monitoring tap in plaintext? If yes, can you provide an example and the mitigation you apply?

3) For escrow/split custody: we need a short summary of the escrow provider (name, country, attestation type) and whether escrow introduces any additional subprocessors with access to key material.

Tom (consultant) also asked if you can provide a statement on retention windows for raw request payloads vs. derived telemetry.

Can we get answers and a small revision to the dataflow that annotates the two risk points (model hosting decryption and telemetry tap) by EOD Friday 6/6? That would keep our internal review on schedule.

Regards,
DPO (Acme Health)

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Acme Health DPO <dpo@acmehealth.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Jill Ramos <jill.ramos@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Jun 2025 14:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SSQ follow-up: KMS custody and subprocessor roles

DPO / Tom / Jill —

Appreciate the specific asks. Below are our responses and the next steps; I reference the attachments Marcus sent and will push an annotated diagram shortly. 

1) Model hosting decryption: model servers do not require customer secret keys to serve deterministic inference. Where cryptographic operations are required (for example, customer-provided embedding encryption or client-side encrypted payloads), decryption happens inside a short-lived, in-memory enclave on the model host and keys are never written to persistent disk. The kms_key_map.csv column "decryption_context" indicates whether a subprocessor performs in-memory-only decryption or persistent access. For Acme's expected usage (text completion + embeddings), only embeddings-at-rest decryption would be relevant if you choose to use CMKs for embeddings storage. We will mark the CSV line for model-hosting as "in-memory ephemeral" and add a short note to the diagram.

2) Monitoring tap: by default we emit only aggregated metrics (latency histograms, error rates, token counts). No plaintext PII is sent to the monitoring pipeline in normal configs. The exceptions are: (a) if a customer enables request-level debug logs; (b) if a customer opts into verbose telemetry for troubleshooting. Both are opt-in and the debug logs are tagged and routed to a customer-scoped bucket with restricted access. We'll annotate the dataflow and add a short paragraph describing the opt-in debug flow and redaction rules.

3) Escrow/split custody: the current escrow prototype uses a third-party HSM provider, VaultSafe Ltd (Ireland, EEA). VaultSafe acts as an escrow agent and does not have routine access to plaintext keys — they hold splitShares and only participate in emergency recovery under the signed process defined in the escrow agreement. We'll include VaultSafe's SOC2 Type II and an HSM attestation summary in the evidence bundle. Escrow does introduce VaultSafe as an additional subprocessor for key recovery; we've listed that in kms_key_map.csv.

Retention windows: raw request payloads are retained by default for 7 days for debugging and billing reconciliation, then truncated to a 24-hour rolling aggregate for metrics. Derived telemetry (metrics/errors) is retained 13 months unless the account selects a shorter retention. If you need a hardened retention SLA (e.g., 30-day raw retention by contract), we can add that to the DPA.

Next steps: Marcus will update the diagram to annotate the two risk points; I'll send the updated redline language for escrow and retention. We'll attach VaultSafe attestation and the revised CSV. Expect the follow-up package within 3 hours.

Thanks —
Monica Patel
Senior Privacy Engineer
Redwood Inference
